hypothesis.statement: The mechanism is now fully decoded and it is a rank question, not a placement question. Both streams allocate the same nine FPRs and the same four scratch slots; the whole 40-word gap is that ours ranks `best_dist` ABOVE every other long-lived web (it takes f6, the top, and pushes d/guard/half/three down to f5/f4/f3/f2) while retail ranks it BELOW everything (it takes f0, the habitual scratch, and the group sits at f6/f5/f4/f3). Frequency does not explain retail's order - its guard has ONE use and sits at f5, above half and three with four uses each - so the ordering is not use-count and not definition order either, since d is defined last and ranks first. The untried axis is the one v2 named and no form of it has been found: make best_dist INTERFERE with the group. The concrete idea not yet tried is to sink the accumulator's initialisation into the loop itself, e.g. seeding `best_idx` to -1 and testing `if (best_idx < 0 || d < best_dist)` - which removes the pre-loop seed entirely - and then checking whether the group forms without it. That form changes the instruction count on its face (it adds a compare), so it is a diagnostic probe rather than a candidate keep, and its VALUE is deciding whether the pre-loop seed load is what enrols best_dist in the group.
